commit_subject: (screen-flagged) b1.6 (PR #1300): removes hard-coded exemplar entry_is_line_a..e derived rules (proof atoms citing other chapters' HTS lines) from every generated chapter and makes them caller inputs; summary claims runtime semantics unchanged — unsure, part of the same decoupling repair.
description: The generated compositions move from the witness's five per-line exemplar flags to membership-semantic caller inputs

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The chapter 26 composition hard-coded its incidence flags to five statistical reporting numbers from other chapters, so the §301 list, §232 metals, reciprocal-annex-exclusion and §338 branches were gated on an HTS number that cannot occur in chapter 26 instead of on the line-list membership the cited provisions define.
triage.triage_notes: Same pattern as index 24 (identical two-hunk shape: summary rewrite plus removal of entry_is_line_a..e). Verified in the post-fix ch26.yaml that entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded (formula: entry_is_line_a) and entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded (formula: entry_is_line_b) plus the §301/§232/§338/Brazil terms still reference the flags, now as caller inputs. Chapter-specific cosmetic variants (redundant parenthesis depth, from vs effective_from spelling) are pre-existing placement-gate devices and unchanged by this commit.
triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this as an architectural decoupling (interface refactor, "runtime semantics unchanged" per the summary) and failed: the diff deletes five derived rules whose formulas were hard-coded equalities against statistical reporting numbers from chapters 22, 72, 76, 85 and 95 inside a chapter-26 composition, so every branch gated on them was false by construction for any chapter-26 entry, and the module's output/input surface changes (the five outputs are removed and the identifiers become caller inputs), which is not mechanical. The pre-state is wrong against the cited source, not merely pilot scope: `entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded` cites the heading 9903.01.32 annex-exclusion note yet was encoded as `entry_is_line_a` (= `hts_number == "7202.11.10.00"`), and reading that note through the pinned release shows the list runs continuously over chapter-99 pages 178-184 and enumerates 21 chapter-26 subheadings (2602.00.00, 2603.00.00, 2606.00.00, 2611, 2612, 2615, 2617, 2620...) alongside the 7202.11.10 line the module picked — so chapter-26 ores that the note excludes were encoded as never excluded. The same pattern gated `china_section_301_component_rate` (whose own atoms cite 9903.88.03 "applies to all products of China that are classified in the following 8-digit subheadings") on those five out-of-chapter lines, which is a condition grounded on the wrong provision; the fix removes it, which is untraceable_branch rather than a missing clause or a boundary/amount error.
triage.verifier_quote:
-  source: HTS 7202.11.10.00 statistical reporting number
-    formula: (((((((((((((hts_number == "7202.11.10.00")))))))))))))
triage.verifier_notes: Runner-up kind is wrong_entity_or_scope (the flags identified the wrong population of entries for this chapter); untraceable_branch fits better because the taxonomy puts "formulas grounded on the wrong provision" there and the fix removes the branch instead of re-scoping it. Three caveats a reviewer should weigh. (1) This commit only deletes the definitions; the referencing formulas (`entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded: formula: entry_is_line_a`, `china_section_301_component_rate`, `section_232_aluminum_component_rate`, `section_338_component_rate`) are byte-identical before and after, so the correction is a re-grounding by deferral to caller-supplied incidence, not a newly encoded membership test inside this module. (2) The identical defect survives this commit in the same file: post-fix line 1951 still has `entry_is_energy_resource` (cited to 9903.01.13 "critical minerals") encoded as `hts_number == "7202.11.10.00"` in the chapter-26 module, so the repair is partial. (3) The summary sentence "This deterministic RuleSpec serialization changes no formula tokens, dates, inputs, proof atoms, or runtime values" is stale boilerplate about the sibling-distinctness parenthesis/prefix treatment; the same paragraph's new text announces the flags are now caller inputs and that "its earlier byte freeze ends with this generator version", and the PR records -500 removed exemplar-flag outputs and witness equivalence only "under input mapping" with an enumerated exception class, so it does not support a mechanical verdict.
